Our long-term study showed significantly better continence scores for the abdominal approach compared with the transanal pull-through. However, stool pattern and enterocolitis scores were somewhat better for the TERPT group (a subgroup of patients undergoing both procedures). These findings raise an important issue about the current surgical management of high distal ileus. We need to continue studying more cases to draw a definitive conclusion on whether these results are due to differences in procedure outcomes or other factors.
